newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan parliament rejects cabinet reshuffle motion.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan parliament rejects cabinet reshuffle motion.

text.p: Taiwan's ruling Nationalist Party blocked an attempt by opposition lawmakers on Friday to raise a motion asking President Lee Teng-hui to replace Premier Lien Chan and order a full cabinet reshuffle.
"The (opposition's) motion was voted not to be raised during today's parliament session," a parliamentary spokesman said.

The parliament rejected a proposal to discuss the opposition's motion by a vote of 74 to 63. The vote came after three cabinet-level ministers resigned on Thursday, increasing pressure on the government ahead of a planned cabinet reshuffle triggered by public discontent over rising crime on the island.
Lien had tendered his resignation earlier in the week. Lee declined to accept, but asked Lien to propose some changes in cabinet positions next week.

Anti-government sentiment erupted after police discovered the naked body of 17-year-old Pai Hsiao-yen, daughter of actress Pai Ping-ping, floating in a river last week. Police said Pai Hsiao-yen had been kidnapped and murdered. Her killers remained at large.
More than 50,000 people marched in Taipei on Sunday to protest against Pai's murder and demand the resignation of Lien and a cabinet reshuffle.
